**The Downloads page gets the Void Deck treatment.** It was the last big screen in Game Mode still wearing Steam's
own colours: a slate-blue gradient behind everything, bright blue progress bars and cyan status text. Now it is
black like the rest of the interface — hairline rules instead of cards, dot-matrix numbers for the percentages and
the time left, and a plain white progress bar where the blue one used to be. The Downloads pop-up, the row in the
bottom bar, the download chip over your library covers and the status screen that shows the game you are pulling
down all follow the same language now.

**The on-screen keyboard loses its blue.** Steam's keyboard themes declare their own colours on the keyboard
element, so tidying the page background alone left the panel slate blue and the keys lit up bright blue when they
were pressed. Void Deck now remaps every colour the keyboard is able to use, so the panel is pure black, the keys
have no boxes or borders, a pressed key inverts to solid ink, and a latched modifier — Shift, Caps, a toggle —
stays filled so you can still see it is on.

**The compatibility badges turn grey.** The platform logos on the game details page carry their own colours, and so
does the rating that tells you whether a game is verified, playable or unsupported. Void Deck is monochrome, so the
artwork loses its hue and the rating drops to muted ink. The rest of the details page is untouched.

**Install / update:** grab `VoidDeck-v1.6.0.zip` from the [v1.6.0 release](https://github.com/endoflineservice/VoidDeck/releases/tag/v1.6.0), or press **Update now** in the Void Deck panel.
